articles.body: Stock market today: Nifty50 and BSE Sensex continued to defy global market trends on Friday, extending their winning streak for the seventh consecutive session. The Sensex surged over 1,700 points, while the Nifty climbed past 25,000 during Friday’s session as early Diwali fireworks went off on Dalal Street.BSE Sensex ended the session at 81,028.02, up 1,718 points or 2.17%. Nifty50 closed at 25,030.35, up 494 points or 2.01%. Global equities suffered a sharp sell-off amid fading enthusiasm for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks following US President Donald Trump’s defeat in the midterm elections.Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited said, “Indian equities defied a global rout, extending their winning run as investors treated the home market as a relatively safe harbour amid turmoil abroad. Wall Street was hammered by a sharp tech sell-off as investors weighed the prospect of tougher regulation under Democrats. Large private banks emerged as the prime beneficiaries, their deep liquidity and attractive valuations making them a natural home for this rotational money.”“A sharp weekly slide in crude, easing US Treasury yields and a firmer rupee further burnished India’s relative appeal. With Fed officials still hinting at further hikes, the US jobs report due later today will be closely watched. Still, as Samvat 2082 draws to a close, the market enters the new Samvat with foreign flows, crude and the currency finally pulling in the same direction,” he added.Why did stock market rally today?FIIs are back D-StreetForeign institutional investors (FIIs) stepped up their purchases of Indian equities on Thursday, recording net buying worth Rs 14,975 crore, according to provisional data from the NSE. This was their largest single-day net investment in many years, as global investors shifted money away from AI-linked trades.FIIs have remained net buyers of Indian stocks on every trading day so far this week. Their buying activity gathered pace in November, although signs of a change in sentiment had emerged in the second half of October.Hopes of relief on the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax front have also brought back investors.Global AI stocks tumbleArtificial intelligence-linked stocks came under heavy selling pressure amid fears of stricter regulation after the Democratic Party defeated President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the US midterm elections, securing control of Congress.The outcome raised concerns that tighter oversight of the AI industry could slow the expansion of AI infrastructure, a key factor behind the stock market rally that has pushed equities to record highs this year.The Nasdaq plunged 6%, marking its steepest decline since the infamous Covid-19 market crash in March 2020. The technology-heavy index also entered correction territory, defined as a fall of 10% from its record closing high on October 6.South Korea’s Kospi, which had come to symbolise the sharp swings associated with the AI-driven market frenzy, was also hit hard. The index plunged more than 9%, triggering a circuit breaker.The global sell-off in AI stocks has, in turn, supported sentiment towards Indian equities, which analysts believe have an ‘anti-AI’ advantage. Veteran banker Uday Kotak recently said he expects India to benefit from the reversal of investment flows as enthusiasm for AI stocks wanes, while the country continues to develop its own AI capabilities.Large-cap stocks riseThe sharp gains on Dalal Street this week follow an extended period of selling that has weighed on investor portfolios since the start of the year. Despite the recent recovery, the Sensex and Nifty continue to trade well below their respective record highs.The decline in stock prices has prompted analysts to highlight attractive valuations across several large-cap companies.Better-than-expected earnings Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) emerged as the biggest gainer on the Sensex, with its shares climbing more than 5% after the automaker reported strong second-quarter earnings.Nomura reiterated its preference for M&M, retaining the company as its top pick and highlighting its strong pipeline of new launches scheduled for 2027. The brokerage said the company's second-quarter performance was broadly in line with its estimates.The ongoing earnings season has delivered results that have generally exceeded expectations, providing additional support to the market rally.“It is important to recognise the fact that this ongoing rally has fundamental support from impressive earnings growth which has come better-thanexpected,” said VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Dhanteras shopping spree may cross Rs 1 lakh crore: What are buyers purchasing this festive season
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: From lightweight gold jewellery to silver coins and traditional decorative items, Dhanteras shopping is seeing demand across categories despite
articles.body: NEW DELHI: From lightweight gold jewellery to silver coins and traditional decorative items, Dhanteras shopping is seeing demand across categories despite precious metal prices remaining significantly higher than last year.Business during the festival is expected to exceed Rs 1 lakh crore nationwide on Friday, with gold and silver purchases alone projected to cross Rs 60,000 crore, according to the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT).The change in buying preferences is particularly visible in the gold jewellery segment. The All India Jewellers and Goldsmith Federation (AIJGF) said jewellers were seeing greater demand for lightweight ornaments in 14-carat and 18-carat categories as consumers looked for options amid high gold prices.Silver, meanwhile, is finding buyers in the form of coins and decorative products. Traditional auspicious items, including figurines of fish, tortoise and elephants, have also seen increased demand, the federation said.While gold prices have come down marginally over the past week, they are still around 20 per cent higher than they were last year. At the time of reporting, 24-carat gold was trading at Rs 1,41,840 per 10 grams.Dhanteras traditionally draws consumers towards purchases of gold, silver and other goods. This year, the higher cost of precious metals has influenced the nature of these purchases, with lightweight jewellery and relatively smaller-ticket items featuring prominently in market demand.CAIT's estimate of more than Rs 1 lakh crore covers the overall trading activity expected across the country during the festival. Gold and silver are projected to make up more than Rs 60,000 crore of this business.The actual sales picture is expected to become clearer later in the day.According to AIJGF, it would issue a detailed press release by the evening after evaluating consumer response and sales trends across markets nationwide. Its assessment will cover the day's performance across gold and silver jewellery, coins and other festive products.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Starlink was last to apply, meet security requirements': Govt defends satcom licensing process
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India welcomes all players in the satellite communications sector, with consumers ultimately deciding which service they want to choose, govt
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India welcomes all players in the satellite communications sector, with consumers ultimately deciding which service they want to choose, govt sources told news agency ANI."Customer is the king," an official told ANI, adding that consumers would make their choice based on pricing, value and quality of services.Currently, three companies hold satcom licences in India: Jio, OneWeb and Starlink. Sources told ANI that tech giant Elon Musk's Starlink was the "last to apply for and receive its licence", but all three companies have been granted licences through a "completely transparent" process.Officials said all three licensees have been asked to demonstrate their capabilities and meet the prescribed security requirements. OneWeb was the first to submit its compliance documents, followed by Jio, while Starlink was the last, as ANI quoted sources.Two key steps remain before services can be rolled out at scale: A decision on spectrum allocation and pricing, and fulfilment of security requirements by all three companies. Once these conditions are met, the satcom ecosystem can benefit as a whole, officials said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pakistan's external debt nearly doubles to $135 billion in 10 years, China biggest lender
articles.summary: Pakistan's external borrowing has nearly doubled in the last 10 years, reaching $135.1 billion in 2025, with China accounting for the largest share of the
articles.body: Pakistan's external borrowing has nearly doubled in the last 10 years, reaching $135.1 billion in 2025, with China accounting for the largest share of the country's outstanding debt among individual creditors.The increase comes as borrowing by developing economies also accelerated, taking the external debt of low- and middle-income countries to a record $9.4 trillion, according to the World Bank's International Debt Report 2026.Pakistan's external debt stood at $68.673 billion in 2015 before rising to $135.107 billion in 2025, Dawn reported, citing the World Bank report.Public and publicly guaranteed borrowing made up the bulk of the debt at $107.076 billion. This was followed by private non-guaranteed debt of $17.58 billion and short-term debt of $10.45 billion.A breakdown of the public and publicly guaranteed component shows that multilateral institutions accounted for $56.83 billion, while bilateral creditors were owed $42.43 billion. Private creditors held claims worth another $7.8 billion.Among individual lenders, China had the highest outstanding exposure to Pakistan at $22.4 billion. The World Bank followed with $19.2 billion, while the Asian Development Bank (ADB) accounted for $16.83 billion.The terms of borrowing also varied considerably depending on the source of credit. Pakistan's loans from official creditors had an average maturity of 16 years and included a four-year grace period. The average interest rate on these loans was 3.6 per cent.Private borrowing was considerably more expensive, carrying an average interest rate of 8.6 per cent. These loans had a three-year repayment period and a one-year grace period.Pakistan also received financial support from key lenders during 2025. China extended the maturities on $2 billion of its loans, while the International Monetary Fund (IMF) made $2.3 billion in fresh disbursements under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility arrangements. These arrangements were aimed at supporting Pakistan's long-term economic stability.The Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (Menap) region recorded improvements in its debt-service and interest ratios. However, its external debt-to-gross national income (GNI) ratio moved in the opposite direction, increasing from 26.7 per cent to 29.4 per cent in 2025.This was the biggest single-year increase in the ratio among all regions, reflecting continued accumulation of external debt.Pakistan's rising debt was part of a wider increase in external borrowing across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Their combined external debt grew 5.5 per cent to $9.4 trillion in 2025, marking the sharpest increase in four years.The expansion was supported by a recovery in bond issuances, a weaker US dollar and renewed interest among private investors in lending to developing economies. This also marked a forceful return of private creditors to these markets.However, access to capital markets came with higher costs, particularly for the poorest countries, which faced some of the highest borrowing costs in decades.Debt-service payments across these economies continued to climb for the fifth year in a row. At the same time, stronger economic growth helped stabilise some debt ratios, while net long-term debt transfers turned positive after several years of outflows.The increase in borrowing was more pronounced among countries eligible for International Development Association (IDA) financing. Their external debt rose 8.1 per cent to $1.3 trillion.Low-income countries recorded an even sharper increase, with external debt climbing 8.9 per cent to $262.4 billion in 2025. This was their biggest increase since 2020.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Gold buying on Dhanteras, Diwali: What should your ideal portfolio look like & what can you buy if not gold?
articles.summary: Are you planning to buy gold on Dhanteras or Diwali this year?
articles.body: Are you planning to buy gold on Dhanteras or Diwali this year? Buying precious metals such as gold and silver is seen to be auspicious during the festive season, but experts caution that investment decisions should focus on portfolio allocation.Within gold investment too, the choices are plenty and each carry their own tax implications.Fundamentally, what needs to be understood is that investors should first assess whether they require gold in their portfolio before investing in it. Although gold has outperformed equities recently, it has also corrected by around 22% from its January 2026 highs.Also Read | Gold price on Dhanteras: 60% return in 2025, 13% in 2026 - what’s the outlook for yellow metal for the next year?What are the factors to consider when making that investment decision? What are the various avenues of gold investment? What can you buy if not gold? We ask experts:What should you do if you have Rs 10,000, Rs 50,000 or even Rs 1 lakh?Gold is often used as a hedge against inflation and market uncertainty. However, it cannot replace equities as a core asset for long-term wealth creation, say experts.“If investors already have sufficient gold exposure, they should avoid adding more to their portfolio. Also, those with a higher than recommended allocation can gradually rebalance it towards diversified equity mutual funds,” says Jasmeet Singh, Executive Director, Anand Rathi Wealth Limited.Sadiya Khan, Chief Investment Solution officer at Mirae Asset Sharekhan says the starting point should be the investor’s objective.“For a retail investor looking to invest Rs 10,000, Rs 50,000 or Rs 1 lakh in gold, gold and gold mutual funds are generally more practical options for portfolio allocation, while coins and jewellery are better suited to physical ownership and gifting. Moreover with gold prices at current level of around Rs 15,000 per gram, an amount of Rs 10,000 or Rs 50,000 may not fetch a meaningful quantity for buying physical gold. This problem of size does not arise with Gold ETFs, gold mutual funds,” she tells TOI.Also, physical gold can involve significant upfront costs. Jewellery making charges can be particularly high, while coins and bars may also be sold at a premium to the prevailing gold value.“For Gold ETFs, investors should look beyond the expense ratio. Trading liquidity, tracking differences and the price at which the ETF trades relative to its indicative NAV can materially affect the actual purchase and sale price.Ultimately, investors should evaluate the total cost of ownership, liquidity, regulatory framework and ease of exit,” she says.“If an investor wants to buy gold for portfolio allocation purposes, Gold ETFs are a suitable option due to their relatively low-cost structure and ease of investment. If an investor wishes to own physical gold, gold coins and bars may be a better option than jewellery, owing to their lower making charges and higher purity and no adjustments made for usage wear and tear,” she adds.Options to buy goldSamit Guha, Managing Director & CEO, MMTC-PAMP notes that consumers today have several ways to buy gold, depending on whether they want physical ownership or a financial-product route.“Physical gold, in the form of jewellery, coins and bars, offers direct ownership and cultural value. Coins and bars add standardised denominations and assured purity, which makes them suited to festive gifting and long-term savings. They need safe storage, so buying from a trusted source matters,” he says.“Gold ETFs are held in a demat account and bought and sold on the exchange. Gold mutual funds offer a similar financial-product route with no physical holding. Digital gold lets consumers build holdings through small, frequent purchases, often with an option to redeem into physical gold, subject to the platform’s terms,” he adds.There are several ways to invest in gold, not just physical gold.Physical gold: This includes jewellery, coins, and bars. These are usually a popular choice during Dhanteras. However, it’s important to remember that jewellery attracts making charges of around 6-25%, along with 3% GST on the total bill. Coins and bars on the other hand carry a smaller premium over the prevailing gold price.Gold ETFs and gold mutual funds allow you to invest in gold without buying or storing it physically. Gold ETFs invest directly in gold bullion, making them a preferred option for gold investment. They are traded on stock exchanges and require a demat account.Gold mutual funds invest in Gold ETFs, do not require a demat account and allow SIPs, but involve double expenses. However, Gold ETFs may trade at a premium to their underlying gold value, so investors should check the price before investing.Digital gold lets you buy gold online in small amounts, with the amount purchased stored in a vault by the provider. However, it is not regulated by SEBI, so it is important to check the credibility of the company offering it.Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are another option, with existing bonds available for purchase on stock exchanges. However, the government has not issued any fresh bonds since February 2024.The tax treatment also varies across these options. Physical gold, digital gold, and gold mutual funds attract long-term capital gains tax when held for more than 24 months, while for Gold ETFs this period is 12 months. Long-term gains are taxed at 12.5%, while short-term gains are taxed at the investor's applicable income tax slab rate.What to buy if not gold?Analysts say that gold buying can often be driven by festive sentiment. It’s important to keep a tab on your overall portfolio mix to make sure it is balanced to meet your goals.According to Jasmeet Singh, long-term investors can consider an 80:20 equity-to-debt allocation.“The equity portion can be invested in actively managed, diversified equity mutual funds, in categories such as large cap, mid-cap, small-cap, large & mid cap, flexi-cap, multi-cap, dividend yield, and focused. The debt allocation can include arbitrage funds for investors in the highest tax bracket and target maturity funds for those in lower tax brackets. Investors can consider allocating half of their debt allocation, amounting to 10%, to Gold ETFs,” Jasmeet Singh says.As an alternative to gold, he recommends debt mutual funds.“Those in the highest tax bracket can consider arbitrage funds while those in lower tax brackets can opt for target maturity funds. These options can help investors preserve portfolio stability while keeping their equity investments focused on long-term wealth creation,” he advises.For Sadiya Khan, REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) and InvITs (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) make for a good alternative bet.REITs allow investors to own units in income-generating real estate assets, while InvITs provide exposure to infrastructure assets such as roads and power transmission projects, offering fractional ownership without buying the assets directly.“These instruments provide investors with tokenized and fractional ownership to real estate and infrastructure assets as an alternative to buying the underlying physical asset. These instruments can offer regular cash flows and portfolio diversification, however, they are subject to market risks, interest rate movements and fluctuations in asset performance,” she explains.“ReITs and InvITs can be volatile, and investors may consider exposure through professionally managed investment products such as mutual funds,” she cautions.She believes that apart from any physical gold requirement, from a portfolio allocation perspective, investors should consider allocating around 5% to 10% of their portfolio to commodities such as gold and silver.“Before determining portfolio allocations across asset classes such as equities, fixed income, gold, and silver, investors should assess their risk profile, investment objectives, investment horizon, and cash flow requirements, or seek expert advice to ensure that their investments are aligned with their financial goals,” she says.“Further, investment in gold must be considered for hedging purposes rather than return generation,” she adds.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production after years of poor sales in few markets
articles.summary: By Ananya Palyekar, Akanksha Khushi and Nick Carey Nov 6 (Reuters) - Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO...
articles.body:
By Ananya Palyekar, Akanksha Khushi and Nick Carey

Nov 6 (Reuters) - Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy ‌pickup trucks that ultimately only sold in just a handful of markets because of its heavy, angular design.

Musk said in an X ‌post the production wind-down would enable the automaker to accommodate increased output of its newly launched Cybercab model, which the billionaire has made central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.

While it was not ​immediately clear whether Cybertruck production would be moved to another facility or phased out entirely, the automaker's Austin plant is the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the model's specialized components.

In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era".

Tesla did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent outside regular business hours.

The US EV maker only began delivering the Cybertruck to customers in late 2023. ‌According to Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold 20,237 Cybertrucks ⁠in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Before the pickup truck launched, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units.

"It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets," said former ⁠Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer. "Every rational auto guy would say the same."

"It will no doubt only be a rounding error on Tesla's balance sheet, but the statistics speak for themselves."

Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Its angular design was mocked by pickup truck purists and ​safety ​experts predicted it would be hard to gain approval for sale in key markets like ​Europe.

The unveiling event itself was marred when Musk tried to ‌prove with a sledgehammer that its windows were shatterproof - only to leave massive cracks in two of them.

During Cybertruck's official launch in 2023, Musk touted it as a futuristic competitor to pickup trucks from General Motors and Ford, saying "finally, the future will look like the future".

But the vehicle has struggled to meet those expectations.

Automotive analyst Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz said that although the Cybertruck has been called a failure because of its poor sales, electric pick-ups from Ford and others have also flopped in the US market.
authors: By Ananya Palyekar, Akanksha Khushi and Nick Carey

articles.title: Spam calls down 99%, crores in fraud blocked: Inside India's massive digital safety push
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The government has prevented nearly Rs 6,500 crore worth of financial fraud and cut daily spam calls by 99% from around 3.5 crore earlier.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The government has prevented nearly Rs 6,500 crore worth of financial fraud and cut daily spam calls by 99% from around 3.5 crore earlier.A key step in preventing financial fraud has been the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), which the Reserve Bank of India has made mandatory for all financial institutions. The system has flagged crores of bank accounts, helping banks identify suspicious activity and stop fraudulent transactions before they happen.Government sources cited by ANI said that nearly Rs 6,500 crore worth of fraud has been prevented through the use of this indicator.The government is also bringing banks, telecom companies and law enforcement agencies together to tackle digital fraud. The Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP), which connects these groups, now has around 1,600-1,800 stakeholders on board. These include banks, law enforcement agencies (LEAs), telecom operators and financial institutions.On the telecom front, daily spam calls have dropped by 99% from around 3.5 crore earlier. The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has also disconnected around 55-56 lakh mobile numbers under its Sanchar Saathi initiative to tackle spam calls and telecom-related fraud.Another measure is Calling Name Presentation (CNAP), which is now in place for all 4G and above subscribers. It allows mobile users to see the caller's name when they receive a call, helping them identify who is calling.Officials said protecting customers from cyber threats remains a key responsibility of the telecom sector. "On cyber security and securing the interests of our customers, we are front line.The Sanchar Saathi initiative has also received a strong response from citizens. Its portal has recorded nearly 35 crore hits, while the mobile application has been downloaded around 3.5 to 4 crore times.The government has said that protecting telecom users and improving cyber security will remain key priorities. "We will not compromise on that."The steps include cutting down spam calls, disconnecting mobile numbers, helping people identify callers and working with banks and law enforcement agencies to prevent financial fraud.You use AI every day. articles.title: Data leaks to cyber frauds: How safe is your money and personal information with banks?
articles.summary: For decades, bank deposits have been a natural choice for people looking to keep their savings safe.
articles.body: For decades, bank deposits have been a natural choice for people looking to keep their savings safe. When gold, real estate and stock markets turn volatile, bank deposits offer a sense of stability, giving people a place to park their money without worrying about market ups and downs.For most savers, it is not so much about earning the highest returns as it is about the comfort of knowing that your hard-earned money is safe.But that sense of trust is now beginning to show cracks.As banking shifts increasingly towards digital platforms, the nature of threats is changing too. Bank thefts are no longer limited to physical break-ins or robberies. Today, money can disappear with just a few clicks, sometimes before customers even realise that something has gone wrong.The risks also go beyond stolen cards and suspicious phone calls. SBI recently flagged 3,897 customer records suspected to have surfaced on the dark web, raising concerns about just how safely banks are guarding customer information. In another case, the Enforcement Directorate searched 19 locations across Haryana and Chandigarh over the alleged embezzlement of Rs 590 crore from Haryana government accounts held with IDFC First Bank.And the list doesn't end there.The CBI arrested a PNB office assistant in Greater Noida and a Pune-based individual over an alleged Rs 10.24 crore fraud at the bank's Pi Sector branch.Clearly, keeping money in a bank may still feel like a safe bet, but keeping it safe is becoming a bigger question.Rs 48,021 crore lost, yet customer trust remains intactAccording to the Reserve Bank of India's Annual Report 2025-26, the amount involved in bank frauds jumped to Rs 48,021 crore in FY26, from Rs 32,803 crore in FY25. Interestingly, the number of reported fraud cases involving Rs 1 lakh and above actually fell to 10,114 in FY26, compared with 23,722 in FY25 and 35,800 in FY24, as per an ET report.But fewer reported cases have not translated into smaller losses. Loan-related frauds accounted for nearly 85% of the total amount involved in FY26, with advances and lending operations emerging as the biggest contributors to both the number of cases and the amount involved.This is a shift from FY24 and FY25, when card, internet and digital payment frauds accounted for the highest number of cases.And the worrying trend goes beyond bank accounts. Data from the Union home ministry's national cybercrime reporting portal and the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System show that more than 53.87 lakh cyber fraud complaints were registered between FY24 and FY26, involving over Rs 56,087 crore.Of this amount, more than Rs 9,079 crore was marked as lien, while just over Rs 206 crore was refunded. The gap between the amount reported as lost and the money refunded shows how difficult it can be for victims to recover their savings.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Despite these concerns, customers have not stopped trusting banks with their money and personal information.An EY report based on a survey of 2,030 banking customers found that 82% trust banks with their data. However, confidence appears less reassuring when it comes to dealing with fraud: only 73% believe banks resolve such cases effectively.Data leaks: How hackers get into your profilesA data leak may not give criminals direct access to bank accounts, but it can provide enough personal information to make targeted fraud more convincing. Banking data can be exposed through cyberattacks on banks or their vendors, phishing, malware, insider misuse and misconfigured systems, Adam Marrè, chief information security officer at Arctic Wolf, a global security operations firm, told TOI.The compromised information can include personal details, account numbers, login credentials, transaction histories and KYC records. Banks' growing dependence on external technology partners creates additional vulnerabilities, says Paramdeep Singh, founder of Long Tail Ventures.“Banking data is compromised through cyberattacks, phishing, insider misuse and vulnerabilities at third-party service providers. The last is particularly concerning given banks’ growing dependence on external technology partners. Leaks typically expose personal details, account information, transaction histories and KYC records. These may not enable direct account access, but can make targeted fraud considerably more convincing.”Criminals can use these details to impersonate bank officials and trick customers into sharing OTPs or approving fraudulent payments.“The data leak creates the opportunity. The fraud often happens through the conversation that follows,” Singh added.The threat also extends to banks, NBFCs and fintech companies. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) and CERT-In have flagged financially motivated cyberattacks involving AI agents, which exploit unpatched software and misconfigured servers to target fund disbursement systems and payment APIs.“Multi-crore unauthorised transactions through fund disbursement systems and APIs are being found in individual cases,” the advisory said.Criminals may route stolen money through mule accounts across banks and quickly transfer or withdraw it using IMPS and NEFT. They may also delete records to hamper investigations.Financial institutions have been asked to report such incidents to CERT-In and the RBI's DAKSH portal within six hours.Are your bank details at risk? Here's when you should sound alarmOne of the biggest challenges with data breaches is that customers may not realise their information has been compromised until someone tries to misuse it. There may be no immediate warning or suspicious transaction to indicate that their details have fallen into the wrong hands.Singh told TOI, “Customers may discover breaches through bank notifications, security alerts or suspicious transactions. Fraudsters combine stolen information with impersonation, using genuine personal details to gain trust before requesting OTPs, payment approvals or account access.”He added, “The data leak creates the opportunity. The fraud often happens through the conversation that follows.”Marrè advised customers to watch for breach notifications, unexpected password-reset requests, unfamiliar account-access alerts and unrecognised transactions.“When a phishing attempt references recent transactions, account details or personal information, it is often far more effective at convincing a victim to disclose additional information or authorize fraudulent transactions,” Marrè added.Beyond immediate financial fraud, exposed information can also be used for identity theft or account takeovers, meaning the risks may persist even when no money is stolen immediately after a breach.Caught in a data breach? Don't wait, act When it comes to banking fraud, waiting to see what happens can prove costly. Whether your personal information has been exposed or you spot an unauthorised transaction, acting quickly is important. Here are the steps customers should take to protect their money and limit further damage:Contact your bank immediately: Report any suspected data breach or unauthorised activity without delay. If your account has been compromised, ask the bank to block affected cards or payment instruments.Change your passwords: If personal information has been exposed, update passwords for potentially affected accounts. Also enable multi-factor authentication for an additional layer of security.Secure your email account: Criminals may use your email to reset passwords or intercept important banking alerts. Change its password and enable multi-factor authentication.Monitor your accounts: Regularly check transactions, login attempts and account changes. Do not ignore even small unfamiliar charges, as criminals may use them to test an account before attempting larger transfers.Report financial cyber fraud: If money has been stolen, call the cyber fraud helpline at 1930 or report the incident at cybercrime.gov.in.Keep a record of complaints: Singh advises customers to file a written complaint and preserve transaction records and acknowledgements. Keep records of all communications with the bank in case the matter needs to be escalated.Approach the RBI Ombudsman if needed: If the bank rejects the complaint, fails to resolve it adequately or does not respond within 30 days, customers can approach the RBI Ombudsman.Continue monitoring your accounts: Reporting an incident does not mean the risk is over. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Karnataka government on Friday alleged that petrol supplied by major oil marketing companies (OMCs) in the state contained ethanol well above the prescribed 20% limit, with laboratory tests recording levels of up to 31.2%. It sought action against companies found supplying fuel with excess ethanol.Food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology minister Rizwan Arshad said petrol samples collected from Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru were tested at Bengaluru-based Shriram Research Institute, which is accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories and ISO-certified, news agency PTI reported.The test results showed ethanol content of 31.2% in Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) petrol and 30.5% in Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) samples. Other samples recorded 27% in HPCL petrol, 26.5% in BPCL Speed, 26.1% in Nayara and 25.5% in Shell petrol. Some samples from BPCL, HPCL and IOCL also recorded levels above 20%, while others ranged from 13.5% to 20.6%.The state government alleged that reports from the in-house laboratories of IOCL and BPCL did not disclose ethanol content, despite it being a prescribed testing parameter."This omission raises serious questions about the transparency of the oil marketing companies and what they seek to conceal from consumers," the release said as quoted by PTI.The government claimed that excess blending could reduce vehicle mileage and damage components such as fuel pumps, injectors, filters, hoses and seals.It said 99% of India's 35 crore vehicles were not designed to run on blends above E20, and sought action against OMCs, compensation for affected consumers, mandatory display of ethanol blend percentages at petrol pumps and a nationwide system offering different fuel blends.It also called for an E20 spoilage fund to compensate consumers for verified vehicle damage.You use AI every day. articles.title: The VIX volatility index just spiked 70%. Here's what history suggests comes next.
articles.summary: Looking for a reason or two to be optimistic after a bruising stock sell-off.
articles.body:
If you are looking for something positive after Thursday's shocking stock beatdown , you have come to the right place ahead of the weekend.

History suggests stocks tend to do well after the extreme volatility we saw two days removed from the Election Day blue wave.

The VIX volatility index ( ^VVIX ) — better known as Wall Street's fear gauge — jumped as much as 70% on Thursday. A move this large has only happened eight times since 1991, according to data from CBOE.

Here's what happened to the S&P 500 on average after the eight prior extreme moves:

1 month later: +3.0% (7 of 8 times positive)

3 months later: +7.1% (6 of 8 times positive)

6 months later: +10.4% (8 of 8 times positive)

1 year later: +14.7% (7 of 8 times positive)

While somewhat comforting, it doesn't exactly erase from the minds what happened in the markets yesterday, as risk was repriced for a Democratic control of the House and Senate.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process. Looked at another way, the total market capitalization of the S&P 500 fell from $68.9 trillion to $65.9 trillion — the largest one-day dollar loss in the index's history.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,830 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ).

"We are now seeing something of a buyers' strike in tech," said Truist chief markets strategist Keith Lerner.

articles.title: Tech just had a crisis-sized day — the kind that came in 2000, 2008, and 2020: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Tech's crisis-sized drop has history on its side, with one big exception.
articles.body:
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell more than 4% Thursday, and tech fell nearly twice as far. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ( XLK ) dropped 8%, its worst day since March 16, 2020, the worst day of the pandemic crash.

The AI trade took the brunt of Thursday's sell-off . Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) fell about 9% to 10%, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) lost 12%.

The S&P 500 tech sector is about 17% below its Oct. 6 record after 22 sessions. About 4% more would mean a bear market , and doing it within two sessions would make it the fastest since 2020, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Only the dot-com and pandemic crashes moved quicker.

XLK's only worse days came in March 2020 and the 2008 financial crisis. Since 1989, the sector has had six earlier drops of 6% or more while near a record. Five blew over fast, with tech falling another 3% to 14% and returning to a record within two to seven months.

The sixth was April 12, 2000. Tech fell another 78% and didn't see a record again until 2017.

Those five came from outside tech, from a failed airline buyout in 1989 to the Asian financial crisis , the Long-Term Capital Management blowup, and the pandemic and tariffs, and most got fast relief from the Fed or Washington. In 2000, the problem was tech itself. This time has a little of both, a political trigger and a worry about tech's own AI spending .

Market breadth is one way Thursday looked more like 2000. On the five crisis days that ended in quick recoveries, at least 8 in 10 S&P 500 stocks fell along with tech. On April 12, 2000, most of its stocks rose even as the index fell about 2%. Thursday landed in between. About 85% of S&P 500 stocks fell, but 74% held up better than the index, according to a Yahoo Finance analysis of Norgate Data.

The Chart Report wrote Thursday that semiconductors "are flashing the same momentum reversal that marked their 2000 top."

While the chart pattern looks familiar, corporate earnings say otherwise. In the year before the March 2000 peak, tech stocks doubled while forward earnings estimates rose 23%. In the year before October's record, prices rose 32%, and estimates jumped 73%. Tech trades at about 24 times forward earnings, versus 62 in March 2000.

Size is where 2026 can hurt like 2000. Tech hit a record 39% of the S&P 500 in October, above its 35% peak in 2000. When tech goes, the index goes with it.

Richard Bernstein, global head of macro and customized investing at Janus Henderson Investors, said the danger is in how momentum ends.

articles.title: Trump doubles down on data centers as he absorbs the market turmoil
articles.summary: President Trump reacted to the volatile Thursday in markets with a series of Truth Social posts overnight, doubling down on his support of data centers and t...
articles.body:
President Trump reacted to the volatile Thursday in markets with a series of Truth Social posts overnight, doubling down on his support of data centers and trying to blame Democrats for the sell-off.

A little after 7 a.m. ET Friday, he renewed his support for data centers , writing he "will work with the many States in the U.S. that want to become RICH by having them" and calling leaders who might be opposed "foolish."

The comments appeared largely directed at Texas, where voters this week elected a new Democratic governor who has promised to halt new data center construction in a race that surfaced deep voter unease over AI and its effects.

Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa pledged on Thursday to protect Texas from data centers via new laws and, in the meantime, would hold off on approving new data center projects "until we have those protections."

Hinojosa defeated outgoing Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, one of the few losing figures Trump has lashed out at this week.

Trump hasn't criticized most losing Republicans but reacted immediately to Abbott's loss , saying the three-term Republican governor would have won if he hadn't become a "RINO" (Republican in name only).

The wave of anti-data center sentiment stretched across the country, elevating Democrats to governorships in places like Ohio and Georgia who could bring a newly critical eye to the sector in the middle of a rapid build-out.

The concerns about a slowdown in data center construction and AI spending led to a steep sell-off in tech stocks on Thursday — ending the worst post-midterm day since 1896 .

Trump tried to pin blame for those losses on Democrats.

"The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame!" Trump posted Thursday night on Truth Social .

A day earlier, he was touting Wednesday's market gains , which came after the Democrats' sweeping win became clear.

Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: The U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, a bright spot for the economy
articles.summary: The U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, a surprisingly strong number that includes what appear to be some AI-related construction and manufacturing jobs.
articles.body: The U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, a surprisingly strong number that includes what appear to be some AI-related construction and manufacturing jobs. American workers have so far seen relatively few benefits from the artificial intelligence boom that has driven the stock market higher and fueled trillions of dollars in spending by the world’s top tech giants. The unemployment rate in October dropped to 4.1%, extending a near-historic low streak. The report “added to evidence of labor-market stability” and consumer resilience, said Jennifer Timmerman, senior investment strategy analyst at Wells Fargo. While that steady figure reflects fulsome employment across the nation, economists also say that it reflects a kind of stagnation. “The problem is the low rate of turnover,” said Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG. “Fewer people are entering the labor force.” Sluggish wage growth did not meaningfully improve last month, however. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year ago, which continues to track well below the rate of inflation. Inflation is 3.7% and on the upswing, as of the most recent consumer price index released Oct. 14. Business inflation is rising even faster, a likely sign of what’s to come for consumers at grocery stores and retail outlets. Friday’s report also showed strong upward revisions to recent jobs data. Net job gains for August were revised up by 53,000, from 133,000 to 186,000. September was revised up by 31,000, from 29,000 positions added to 60,000, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said in a statement. The report was “a blowout,” said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. But she cautioned that any impact from the additional jobs would be blunted by other economic headwinds. It “doesn’t erase this painful fact: Inflation has wiped out all wage gains for 7 straight months,” Long wrote on X. “In fact, the inflation resurgence has been so strong that it’s basically wiped out all wage gains since January 2025.” Friday’s jobs report also suggests the sprawling AI data center buildout across the country could be supporting at least some construction and manufacturing jobs. Manufacturing roles in October rose by 19,000 last month, according to BLS data. The sector has added more than 100,000 jobs total since its recent low, in December 2025. The agency noted that within the manufacturing sector, the subsets of computer and electronics manufacturing, machinery manufacturing and what it called “primary metal manufacturing” led the gains. Nonresidential construction jobs also jumped by almost 3,000 roles in October, likely an indication of demand for data center jobs. In contrast to the commercial construction industry, the home building and contracting sector shed more than 15,000 jobs last month. High interest rates have paralyzed the residential real estate market and cut demand for the kind of refinancing loans that typically fund home renovations. Other sectors that have been largely powering U.S. job growth for years also showed strong gains in the month. The healthcare sector added 42,000 jobs, which the BLS said was higher than its average monthly gain over the past year. The professional and business services sector, as the agency classifies it, gained 70,000 jobs, blowing past its average monthly gain of 15,000 over the past year. Retailers also appear to have started strong holiday hiring, with firms classified as “general merchandise retailers” adding more than 18,000 roles. Friday’s data also bolstered the case for an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve when it meets Dec. 8 and 9. Following the BLS release, the odds of a December interest rate hike jumped to nearly 80%.

articles.title: Why SoftBank stock is sinking under the weight of its AI bets
articles.summary: The rout in tech-focused SoftBank is getting alarming.
articles.body:
The over-the-top tech house Masayoshi Son has spent billions to build at SoftBank ( SFTBY ) is getting torched, looking at the stock price action.

SoftBank shares crashed 10.83% in early trading on Friday after losing 14.4% on Thursday as the AI-heavy company was swept into the broader AI stock rout. Sentiment was also dinged by an FT report that China would not allow SoftBank to go ahead with the $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics division.

The company's credit risk climbed to its highest level in four years today, as measured by its five-year credit default swap (CDS) spread. The spread widened to as much as 466 basis points, its highest since Oct. 22, Reuters reported.

The level indicated a default probability of 30.6%.

SoftBank's primary asset anchor remains its roughly 90% ownership stake in Arm Holdings ( ARM ), whose chip architectures power the vast majority of mobile and enterprise AI workloads. With concerns about a "blue wave" on Election Day stunting AI demand , a company like Arm is caught in the crosshairs — and by extension so is SoftBank.

Meanwhile, the company also has a $64.6 billion stake in OpenAI, which had decided to push its IPO out to 2027. But OpenAI's valuation is at risk in light of the blue wave, as seen in chatter that the upcoming Anthropic IPO won't deliver it a $2 trillion valuation as many expected.

articles.title: Fox Closes $22 Billion Roku Takeover, Says Streaming Platform Will Remain ‘Open Ecosystem’
articles.summary: Surprise! Fox Corp. said Friday it has closed the acquisition of streaming platform Roku, a deal valued at $22 billion, well ahead of the expected 2027 date....
articles.body:
Surprise! Fox Corp. said Friday it has closed the acquisition of streaming platform Roku, a deal valued at $22 billion, well ahead of the expected 2027 date.

Roku founder and CEO Anthony Wood will join the Fox board of directors. He will serve as co-chair, Fox Digital Platforms, a newly formed division that includes Roku, Tubi, Fox One, Red Seat Ventures and other digital products and services across the company, alongside Paul Cheesbrough, who assumes the role of co-chair and CEO of the division.

"The closing of this acquisition advances the long-term strategy of Fox," Lachlan Murdoch, executive chair and CEO of Fox Corp., said in a statement Friday.

Fox Corp. emphasized its pledge that it will preserve Roku "as a leading open ecosystem for the broader streaming industry." That means that, say, it won't give exclusive or advantageous positioning to Fox News or the Fox One streaming package on Roku, which has a customer base of more than 100 million households.

The Roku deal will dramatically beef up Fox's streaming footprint and give it the opportunity to increase scale in the free, ad-supported streaming space through Fox's Tubi and the Roku Channel. With Roku, Fox overnight is now a much bigger player in digital video advertising as well as key distributor of premium subscription streaming services.

"Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform," Murdoch said. "Our shared entrepreneurial passion and clear conviction toward building the future together with our new Roku colleagues gives us great confidence in the opportunities ahead of us."

Fox Corp. said it expects to achieve approximately $400 million of annualized cost synergies within two years after the Roku deal close, suggesting layoffs are in the offing. Fox also said there's potential revenue upside with the combination of Roku's business and that it anticipates that the acquisition will be accretive to free cash flow per share by the second full year after closing.

Wood said in a statement: "We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn't change today. What does change is our reach and resources. Fox has a deep respect for Roku's culture and wholly shares our commitment to staying open to every content partner. Our teams will keep building and innovating as they always have, now with the support and capabilities of Fox behind us. I'm proud of what Roku's employees have built, and I'm excited about what comes next."

articles.title: Georgia is the 'underappreciated risk' for data center backlash
articles.summary: Keep your eyes on this key AI state in the wake of the midterm elections.
articles.body:
The AI trade has kept its eyes on the data center-heavy state of Texas in the wake of the midterm election blue wave that saw data center critic Gina Hinojosa take over as governor from Republican Greg Abbott.

But investors would be wise to pay equal — or more — attention to Georgia to see how the political winds are blowing for data centers there.

"Georgia may be the underappreciated risk," Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei said, adding that "Atlanta has become an extremely popular market with big investment from a range of credible developers, including both Digital Realty Trust ( DLR ) and Equinix ( EQIX )."

Rezaei noted that the Georgia Public Service Commission flipped to a 3-2 Democratic majority, giving Democrats control of the body that decides who pays for power and how quickly it arrives.

Major approvals, including approximately 10 gigawatts of certification and OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) 3.2GW contract, are already complete, Rezaei noted. But Georgia Power's next capacity request and 2028 rate case remain outstanding.

"What the new majority can reach is the future: Georgia Power's next capacity request (for 2032-33, filed mid-2027) and the 2028 rate case," Rezaei said. "That makes it a pricing lever on 2030s load, not a stop sign on today's construction. The exposure is concentrated in a handful of campuses: OpenAI's Camellia (3.2 GW nameplate), DLR's Project Bunkhouse (2.0 GW), QTS in Blakely (1.4 GW) and Google's White Oak and Rumble sites (2.7 GW combined). Most of it is back-end loaded, with 87% of Georgia's pre-construction credible capacity dated 2029 or later. The equipment sales-tax exemption runs through 2031, and repealing it still needs a Republican Senate. Bottom line: Georgia didn't really get riskier this year, but it did get more expensive later."

The markets are on edge over fears that a slowdown in data center build-outs will upset the profit boom of the world's biggest companies — all of which are in tech.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 4.4% of its market value on Thursday , wiping out $3 trillion in the process.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) plunged 1,280 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) cratered 4.8%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ).

Hinojosa just dropped a sign of what's to come for data centers.

"We have always been a pro-business state in Texas, but what changes now with me as governor is it has to be a partnership that benefits Texans," Hinojosa said in a CNN interview late Thursday. "And right now what has happened is data centers have moved into mostly rural communities, and there are no rules and laws to protect Texans, and Texans are being taken advantage of. So the difference is we will have laws to protect Texans, and we need to stop what we are doing with data centers until we have those protections. It is not that I hate data centers. I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas, and that stops when I'm governor."

articles.title: Trump to tape ‘60 Minutes’ interview after GOP midterm rout
articles.summary: President Donald Trump is scheduled to tape a post-election interview this morning for Sunday’s “60 Minutes.”
articles.body: President Donald Trump is scheduled to tape a post-election interview this morning for Sunday’s “60 Minutes.” The sit-down will be Trump’s first in-depth interview since the Republican Party’s sweeping midterm losses on Tuesday. And it will be a high-profile one: “60 Minutes” is the highest-rated newsmagazine on American TV. CBS News sources confirmed the interview plan but cautioned that it hasn’t taken place yet. Friday’s White House schedule says Trump will participate “in a pre-tape interview” at 10:30 a.m. Eastern. The interviewer is Ross Douthat, the former New York Times columnist who recently joined “60 Minutes” as a correspondent. Douthat, a conservative who has frequently been critical of Trump, previously interviewed Vice President JD Vance for his Times podcast. In a column earlier this week, Douthat depicted the midterms as a failure of “the New Right.” Trump has a long and complex history with “60 Minutes.” He last appeared on the program in April, in the immediate aftermath of the shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner. That interview, with Norah O’Donnell, became contentious; Trump called ‘Donnell a “disgrace” and said, “You’re horrible people.” Trump certainly cares a lot about “60 Minutes,” as evinced by the occasional critiques he posts on Truth Social. And he is well aware that the program is high-rated. Last Sunday’s episode averaged 10 million viewers, buoyed by an NFL game lead-in. Trump refused to sit down for a traditional pre-election interview on “60 Minutes” in 2024. But his opponent Kamala Harris did, and Trump then sued CBS over the interview, claiming it was deceptively edited. Legal experts said the suit was frivolous, but the owners of CBS at the time decided to pay Trump to make the matter go away. They agreed to a $16 million settlement, sparking outrage across the news industry. The lawsuit and settlement roiled the tight-knit “60 Minutes” team. And it was just the start; once the Ellison family took control of CBS last year, Bari Weiss took over CBS News and turned her attention to “60 Minutes,” upsetting its fiercely independent culture. Last spring Weiss forced out the newsmagazine’s top producers and several correspondents and installed tech journalist and filmmaker Nick Bilton as executive producer. Weiss and Bilton hired a raft of new correspondents and contributors, including Douthat, who had interviews with the Senate candidates in Michigan on last weekend’s broadcast. CBS News and CNN are both owned by Skydance.

articles.title: Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher following worst sell-off since 2020
articles.summary: Nvidia, AMD, Micron, and Sandisk rebounded on Friday after the chip sector suffered its worst daily drop since 2020.
articles.body:
Chip stocks rebounded on Friday after suffering their worst sell-off since 2020. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) bounced 4% following a 12% plunge on Thursday.

Shares of US chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) jumped nearly 6%, erasing part of their 10% slide in the prior session. AMD ( AMD ) also rebounded 9% after suffering a 17% fall. Nvidia ( NVDA ), which declined 9% in the prior session, jumped 4%.

Semiconductors bounced back after much of the AI trade was hammered on Thursday as investors digested what a Democratic win in Congress means for the data center build-out in the US.

Memory and storage names Sandisk ( SNDK ), Micron Technology ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) shares tumbled alongside Samsung Electronics ( 005930.K S ) following Thursday's wipeout on Wall Street.

Other notable movers rebounding on Friday include processor maker Qualcomm ( QCOM ) and chip designer Arm Holdings ( ARM ).

articles.title: Hical raises $30-40 mn from Premji Invest
articles.summary: Hical Technologies raises $30-40M from Premji Invest to expand manufacturing in South India, boost R&D, and scale aerospace and defence exports.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Aerospace and defence components maker Hical Technologies has raised $30-40 million from Premji Invest, the family investment office of Wipro founder Azim Premji, in its first institutional funding round since being founded in 1986.The Bengaluru-based company said the money will fund manufacturing expansion across South India and strengthen engineering and research and development. It is building a new facility in Hosur and recently opened another in Devanahalli.Exports account for more than 90% of Hical’s business, the company said. Its products include motors, actuators, solenoids and transformers used in aircraft, defence equipment and space applications.Hical supplies Dassault Aviation for the Rafale fighter jet programme. It also makes more than 1,000 types of parts used in Boeing and Airbus commercial aircraft and business jet applications, according to the company. Its components are also used in ISRO launch vehicles, satellite applications and ship and submarine equipment.“Our ambition is to build from India for the world, not simply by adding capacity, but by increasing the engineering and technology content of what we deliver,” said Yashas Jaiveer, managing director of Hical Technologies.The company plans to take on more complex systems involving greater design work. The expansion will include high-precision machinery and specialised aerospace manufacturing processes, with the Hosur facility adding precision machining capacity. Part of the investment will also go towards technical staff and quality systems.Premji Invest partner Manoj Jaiswal said global aerospace and defence supply chains were increasingly looking for engineering and manufacturing partners in India, creating an opportunity for Hical to expand.Hical has served the aerospace and defence sector for more than two decades. Deloitte Corporate Finance acted as its exclusive financial adviser on the transaction. The company did not disclose its valuation or the stake acquired by Premji Invest.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'A blowout': US added 165,000 jobs in October, trouncing expectations
articles.summary: Economists expected a gain of 70,000 jobs last month.
articles.body:
The US added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past economists' expectations, as the labor market showed strength despite the Federal Reserve's recent rate hikes.

The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1% even amid a slight increase in labor force participation. September's underwhelming jobs report of 29,000 additions was also revised upward to a gain of 60,000 jobs.

Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, deemed the results "a blowout" in a post on X .

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg projected a gain of about 70,000 jobs in October and saw the unemployment rate holding steady. Wage growth increased 0.4% from September, better than expectations for 0.3% month-over-month growth. Annual earnings rose 3.1%, beating expectations but likely still below the current inflation rate.

Employers added jobs in a number of sectors of the economy. Professional and business services, which had been seen as more vulnerable to AI-related disruptions, added 70,000 roles. Healthcare, long a strong spot for job growth, added a higher-than-average 42,000 positions.

Transportation and warehousing jobs rose by 25,000, and manufacturing continued to show strength with 19,000 additions.

"This is still a low-hire, low-fire market overall, but we could be seeing some green shoots on the hiring side," Jake Krimmel, senior economist at Realtor.com, said in a statement.

Other job market measures released earlier this week telegraphed steady hiring — though not to the extent of Friday's report blowout number. Job openings and hiring edged higher , the Labor Department's monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey showed; private employers added 86,000 jobs , according to ADP; and layoff plans dropped to a three-year low while seasonal hiring ramped up.

"Consistent with prior, more partial indicators of the US labor market, the October Jobs Report came in very strong, across the board," Wharton economist Mohamed El-Erian posted on X.

The solid report will likely give the Federal Reserve more confidence to move forward with another rate hike in December . The central bank will also consider November jobs data and October's inflation figures before its Dec. 9 rate decision. Traders currently see a 77% chance of a 25 basis point rate hike next month, up from 67% on Thursday, according to CME FedWatch.

"Today's jobs report is a strong rebuttal to fears that the economy is heading into a meaningful slowdown," Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management, said in a statement. "With wage growth also picking up, a December Fed hike remains firmly on the table despite the recent tightening in financial conditions."

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Airbnb stock jumps as company reenters 'growth mode,' plans to develop its own AI agent
articles.summary: Airbnb stock jumped 10% on Friday after the peer-to-peer home rental company touted strong growth across its business and raised its full-year outlook amid h...
articles.body:
Airbnb ( ABNB ) stock jumped nearly 10% on Friday after the peer-to-peer home rental company touted strong growth across its business and raised its full-year outlook amid robust global travel demand.

"Airbnb is back in growth mode," CEO Brian Chesky said in a release to investors. "It's rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that's exactly what we're doing. In Q3, we delivered our fastest revenue growth in more than three years, with acceleration across our business, including our most established markets."

In the third quarter, Airbnb reported earnings per share of $3.16, surpassing Wall Street analyst estimates of $2.85 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Revenue grew 19% to $4.87 billion, also beating estimates of $4.74 billion.

"In North America, nights booked grew at their fastest pace in four years," Chesky said. "We're also seeing more guests return to Airbnb, and more people try it for the first time."

The company's strong quarter led it to raise its guidance for the remainder of the year.

In the fourth quarter, Airbnb expects revenue to grow 16% to 19% to a range of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, exceeding the Street's midpoint estimate of $3.16 billion.

For the full year, Airbnb forecasts revenue growth in the high teens and an increase in adjusted EBITDA margin to approximately 36%.

On the earnings call, Chesky outlined plans for Airbnb to build its own AI agent to help people book travel.

He laid out the advantages to this approach, noting that Airbnb understands its marketplace better than any general-purpose AI agent and can make changes to reservations more easily than an outside AI agent.

"Perhaps most importantly, we're building a new interface specifically for travel," Chesky said. "We don't think the traditional chatbot is the right way to plan travel. It's the wrong interface. So what we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for … This is going to feel a little bit like generative UI in the sense that it's going to offer up the right interface at the right time for your specific travel needs."

articles.title: Iren stock rebounds as company's Q1 AI cloud revenue surges
articles.summary: Iren shares rebounded on Friday as the provider of AI compute capacity reported a surge in its fiscal Q1 cloud revenue.
articles.body:
Iren ( IREN ) stock surged on Friday as the data center operator reported strong growth in its artificial intelligence cloud business in its fiscal first quarter.

Iren shares jumped as much as 19% in early trading Friday, rebounding from a roughly 17% decline in the previous session amid a broader sell-off in the AI trade . Despite the recovery, Iren shares remain down more than 50% year to date as investor concerns over AI infrastructure spending, financing requirements and data center expansion have weighed on the sector. The company, which has transitioned from bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) mining into AI cloud and data center infrastructure, has been particularly affected by the recent pullback in neocloud stocks.

Iren, whose customers include Microsoft ( MSFT ), reported $200 million in AI revenue during the three months ending Sept. 30, up from $71 million in the previous quarter and $7 million in the year-earlier period.

However, the company posted a quarterly loss of $263 million, wider than the average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg.

Iren's AI Cloud gross margin of 86% came in line with the prior quarter.

Iren said it expanded an existing agreement with a leading frontier AI lab and separately signed a new five-year contract under which the customer prepaid approximately 90% of the associated GPU costs, reducing the need for additional debt financing.

The company also pushed back its timeline for reaching a $4 billion annualized revenue target, now expecting to hit the milestone in January or February, compared with its previous December forecast. The delay reflects supply constraints affecting critical equipment as well as a design change requested by Microsoft that has slowed development of a data center project in Texas.

articles.title: Bosch Q2 revenue rises 28%, net profit up 19%
articles.summary: Bosch Q2 FY27: Revenue rises 28% to Rs 7,655 crore, net profit up 19% to Rs 840 crore, boosted by automotive demand and Bosch Chassis consolidation.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Bosch reported a 19% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit at Rs 840 crore for the September quarter of FY27, driven by strong demand across automotive segments and the inclusion of Bosch Chassis Systems India in its consolidated results for the first time.Consolidated revenue from operations rose 28.2% to Rs 7,655 crore, compared with the corresponding quarter of the previous year.The company recognised an exceptional gain of Rs 130 crore during the quarter following a reassessment of its service award liability and reversal of the corresponding provision.The growth was largely driven by the automotive business, whose overall product sales increased 29.8% year-on-year. Power Solutions grew 36.4%, while Vehicle Motion recorded growth of 34.9%. The two-wheeler business expanded 17.7%, supported by a favourable product mix and increased demand from original equipment manufacturers ahead of the festive season.The mobility aftermarket business grew 13.2%, while the Beyond Mobility business reported 24% growth in net sales, driven by demand in the Power Tools segment.Bosch’s consolidated results include the performance of Bosch Chassis Systems India, its wholly owned subsidiary, for the first time following its acquisition during the quarter.On a standalone basis, revenue from operations increased 28.6% to Rs 6,164 crore. Standalone net profit stood at Rs 675 crore.Guruprasad Mudlapur, president of the Bosch Group in India and managing director of Bosch, said performance was driven by steady demand across vehicle segments and positive market momentum during the festive season.You use AI every day. articles.title: Did Amazon owe you a refund? You may qualify for part of a $300 million settlement.
articles.summary: Amazon customers who failed to receive refunds or were incorrectly charged for returned merchandise may be eligible for payments under a $309.5 million class...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Amazon customers who failed to receive refunds or were incorrectly charged for returned merchandise may be eligible for payments under a $309.5 million class-action settlement.

While some Amazon ( AMZN ) settlement payments were issued automatically, others have until Dec. 1, 2026, to file a claim.

The fund is part of a broader settlement that topped $1 billion. That total includes roughly $600 million in refunds that Amazon has already issued. The final approval hearing is scheduled for March.

What the Amazon returns settlement is about

The settlement stems from a 2023 class action lawsuit that alleged Amazon failed to properly process refunds for returned products for nearly nine years.

While "Amazon promises customers 'free, no hassle returns,' it routinely … fails to issue refunds or re-charges customers who have returned items in compliance with Amazon's refund and exchange policies because of defects in Amazon's return and refund processes, often incorrectly claiming that the return had not been received by Amazon," the lawsuit claims.

Plaintiffs also alleged that Amazon believed "customers did not notice" the return failures, some of which resulted from "human error."

Amazon denied any wrongdoing, and as part of the settlement, changed some of its return and refund operations for up to two years. Among the changes, the online retailer agreed to monitor return processing times and notify customers when refunds are approved or denied.

Amazon customers are eligible for the settlement payout if they initiated a return or refund for a physical product between Sept. 5, 2017, and Feb. 12, 2026, and did not receive a refund, the refund was delayed or for an incorrect amount, or they received a refund and then were later incorrectly charged again for the returned product.

A final settlement court hearing will be held on March 16, 2027.

How much are the refund settlement payments?

No average payments have been reported so far, and each payout varies based on the amount of unpaid, late, or reversed refunds.
